yearPolicy: Latest shared reporting vintage with same-year indicator and population observations in both access series in every project language set. Missing countries are excluded, not filled from other years or treated as zero.
estimateNote: Project-defined language sets. Counts are estimated as population × (1 − access percentage / 100); proportions are weighted by the population of countries with both observations. These are not official UN/ITU/JMP language-region totals. Sets may overlap and must not be added together.

definitions.thirst: Safely managed drinking water: an improved source on premises, available when needed, and free from faecal and priority chemical contamination. Its complement does not mean no drinking water or no basic water service.
definitions.offline: Internet use: using the Internet from any location in the last three months. Its complement is non-use under this statistical definition, not an observed real-time connection failure.

metadata.name: People using safely managed drinking water services (% of population)
metadata.sourceNote: The percentage of people using drinking water from an improved source that is accessible on premises, available when needed and free from fecal and priority chemical contamination. Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.

metadata.sourceNote: Internet users are individuals who have used the Internet (from any location) in the last 3 months. The Internet can be used via a computer, mobile phone, personal digital assistant, games machine, digital TV etc.
